description: Harden the worker Dockerfile Node.js tarball download with SHASUMS256 sha256 verification and curl retry, failing closed on mismatch.

officialDocsConsulted.summary: Confirmed SHASUMS256.txt lists BARE filenames (no directory prefix), e.g. node-v22.23.1-linux-x64.tar.xz and node-v22.23.1-linux-arm64.tar.xz. sha256sum -c therefore requires the tarball to sit in cwd under its exact bare filename, not /tmp/node.tar.xz.

userStories.title: Verify Node tarball sha256 against SHASUMS256.txt with retrying curls
userStories.description: As the operator of the worker container image, I need the Node.js tarball download to be checksum-verified against nodejs.org's published SHASUMS256.txt (and both curls to retry on transient network flakes) so that a corrupted, truncated, or flaky download fails the build closed instead of extracting a bad toolchain.
acceptanceCriteria: The Node install RUN block in .devcontainer/Dockerfile downloads the tarball to its real bare filename node-v${NODE_VERSION}-linux-${NODE_ARCH}.tar.xz (not /tmp/node.tar.xz), fetches https://nodejs.org/dist/v${NODE_VERSION}/SHASUMS256.txt, selects the line for that bare filename, and runs sha256sum -c on it before any tar extract. [oracle: file-assert grep -q 'SHASUMS256.txt' .devcontainer/Dockerfile && grep -q 'sha256sum -c' .devcontainer/Dockerfile]

The checksum selection keys off ${NODE_ARCH} (the variable derived from dpkg --print-architecture in the same RUN block), never a hardcoded x64, so both amd64 (x64) and arm64 builds verify their own artifact. [oracle: file-assert grep -q 'node-v${NODE_VERSION}-linux-${NODE_ARCH}.tar.xz' .devcontainer/Dockerfile]

The tar extract line is updated to consume the real filename node-v${NODE_VERSION}-linux-${NODE_ARCH}.tar.xz (the prior tar -xJf /tmp/node.tar.xz path no longer exists), and the checksum check precedes the extract so a mismatch stops the build with a non-zero exit and no extraction. [oracle: file-assert ! grep -q '/tmp/node.tar.xz' .devcontainer/Dockerfile]

Both curls (the Node tarball and SHASUMS256.txt) retain --fail and add retry flags (--retry with a small count plus --retry-connrefused and --retry-delay) so a transient network flake retries instead of failing the build. [oracle: file-assert grep -q -- '--retry' .devcontainer/Dockerfile && grep -q -- '--retry-connrefused' .devcontainer/Dockerfile]

The RUN block remains a single-arch build (no buildx / --platform / TARGETARCH introduced); NODE_ARCH still comes from the existing dpkg --print-architecture case statement. [oracle: file-assert ! grep -q 'TARGETARCH' .devcontainer/Dockerfile]
Typecheck passes (bun run typecheck). [oracle: bun run typecheck]
Lint/static spine passes (bun run check:all). [oracle: bun run check:all]

The ci-container job (.github/workflows/ci.yml) builds the worker image successfully on the container_changed=true path (this change touches .devcontainer/**), exercising the new verification step end-to-end on a real Docker build. [oracle: named-command bun scripts/test-in-container.ts]
userStories.notes: Single-file change: .devcontainer/Dockerfile lines 37-49 (the ARG NODE_VERSION RUN block). GOTCHAS (from issue spec): (1) SHASUMS256.txt lists BARE filenames (confirmed via fetch) so the tarball MUST be downloaded to node-v${NODE_VERSION}-linux-${NODE_ARCH}.tar.xz in the working dir, not /tmp/node.tar.xz, or sha256sum -c mismatches on filename; update the tar -xJf path (Dockerfile:45) to match. (2) grep/select MUST use ${NODE_ARCH} not hardcoded x64 or arm64 breaks. (3) Build is single-arch per invocation (buildDockerBuildArgv in src/supervisor/worker-container.ts:231-253 emits plain docker build, no buildx). (4) NO test asserts Dockerfile text; the real oracle is the ci-container image build succeeding (macOS ci job has no Docker daemon - CAM-178 trap - so local `bun test` alone does NOT exercise the build). CI will not deliberately corrupt the tarball, so fail-closed is confirmed by inspection of ordering (checksum before extract). (5) No existing --retry / sha256sum -c convention in the repo; this is the first, consistent with the pinned-reproducible-toolchain intent in the Dockerfile header (lines 1-13, 33-35). OUT OF SCOPE (rejected on merit in the issue): GPG signature verification, base-image digest pinning (Dockerfile:16), the claude-code npm install hash (Dockerfile:58), apt signing (Dockerfile:26-31). Strictly the Node tarball. This story does NOT touch vendor/ or templates/, so no embed-vendor check needed.
